title: Request-level observability shim for adaptive OTLP-to-Prometheus routing and trace enrichment
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Implement a lightweight request-level shim that sits at the ingress/router layer to enrich OTLP spans/metrics with request context, apply adaptive cardinality rules, and route telemetry either to Prometheus-compatible exporters (high-cardinality pruned metrics) or to the long-term OTLP pipeline (raw/trace-forwarded).

Background and motivation:
- Current telemetry path sends high-cardinality labels (route, model_version, prompt_tag, customer_route_id) directly into the long-term metrics pipeline, causing storage blowups and expensive queries.
- Many downstream dashboards (per-route latency/error SLOs) require near-real-time Prometheus-style metrics with bounded label cardinality for efficient querying.
- We also need richer trace hooks to capture per-request decoding/tokenization/cold-start contributions that aren't available in existing spans.

Scope of this ticket:
- Build an Observability Shim service (lightweight, horizontally scalable) deployed as sidecar/ingress filter that will: 1) consume per-request OTLP spans/metric envelopes, 2) enrich them with router-level fields (route_id, model_variant, tenant_type, kv_cache_hit), 3) apply adaptive label pruning and aggregation rules configured per-tenant and per-route, 4) forward pruned metrics to a Prometheus push-adapter and optionally forward raw traces/selected spans to OTLP long-term ingestion.

Key design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Where to run enrichment: sidecar vs centralized aggregator. We chose an in-path shim (edge filter / ingress sidecar) to ensure we capture request routing metadata reliably and to enable tenant-specific adaptive policies with minimal additional context propagation. This reduces cross-service joins but adds a small CPU/latency footprint at the edge.
- Cardinality control model: deterministic label hashing + soft cap. We will compute a hashed label bucket for free-form labels (e.g., prompt_tag) and only emit the top-k explicit values per-bucket per-window; remaining values are folded into an "other" bucket. This preserves signal while bounding cardinality.
- Sampling and fidelity: traces will be sampled according to existing sampling policy, but the shim will create lightweight synthetic spans for tokenization/decoding/cold-start time when the original trace is sampled out, enabling lower-fidelity but still useful breakdown metrics in Prometheus.
- Routing policy: latency-sensitive metrics for production routes go to Prometheus (fast scraping/alerting); heavy raw telemetry for debugging or audit customers is routed to OTLP storage (higher cost). Policies are tenant-configurable and policy decisions are recorded as events for traceability.

Implementation notes / schema mapping:
- Input: OTLP v1 envelopes + HTTP request metadata (route headers).
- Enrichment fields added: route_id, model_version, shard_pool, deployment_zone, kv_cache_hit (boolean), tenant_class (self-serve | enterprise), request_priority.
- Output metric families: request_duration_seconds (histogram with bounded buckets), request_error_count (counter), kv_cache_hit_ratio (gauge per-route aggregated), decode_time_seconds (histogram), token_emit_rate (gauge). All exported metrics must follow the prometheus-safe label set (max 20 labels by default).
- Config: policy store in Config Service (featureflag + per-tenant overrides). Shim fetches policy on startup and subscribes to deltas.

Rollout plan and safety guards:
1) Unit tests + integration harness against local OTLP/Prometheus push adapters.
2) Internal canary: enable shim for staging routes only with strict sampling (1%) and strict label caps to validate correctness and compare metrics to baseline.
3) Gradual ramp-up to low-traffic production routes (10% traffic) with continuous comparison dashboards (raw vs pruned).
4) Full rollout gated by: metric drift < 3% for core SLOs, no increase in 95th latency <= 5ms at ingress, storage cost projections OK.

Observability & dashboards required by end of rollout:
- Side-by-side latency/error dashboard comparing shim-exported Prometheus metrics vs raw OTLP aggregates per-route.
- Cardinality heatmap for labels over time to detect label explosions and policy effectiveness.
- Shim health: processing latency, queue backlog, policy sync errors, per-tenant reject rates.

Longer-term follow-ups (out of scope but tracked):
- User-configurable schema templates for customers to define which free-form labels are high-value.
- Integrate with Optimize to recommend per-route label caps based on query workloads.
- Persistent identity mapping service for remapping hashed buckets back to canonical values during investigative workflows.
acceptance_criteria: Shim service accepts OTLP envelopes and enriches with router metadata for a test set of routes
Adaptive cardinality pruning enforces configured cap and returns 'other' bucket for overflow during a high-cardinality stress test
Shim exports Prometheus-compatible metrics (histogram/counter/gauge) to the push adapter and we can graph same-day latency SLOs in Grafana
Synthetic trace hooks created for tokenization/decoding/cold-start when original trace is not sampled and those metrics appear in Prometheus
Policy delta pushes are consumed by shim without restart and reflected within 60s in emitted metrics
No input p99 processing latency regression > 5ms at ingress under baseline load in staging

comments: 2026-03-02 Aisha Kumar: Kickoff meeting notes - decided to keep enrichment at router to avoid cross-service propagation complexity. Action: Marcus to prototype sidecar in 1 week.

2026-03-04 Marcus Li: Prototype working against local OTLP sink. Observed ~1.8ms median overhead on a small payload; added fast-path to bypass heavy hashing if tenant is enterprise and policy set to raw-forward.
2026-03-05 Review by Priya Nair (SRE): Requested a hard CPU budget per shim and fallback to central aggregator when budget exceeded. Added task to enforce cgroups and backpressure signaling.
2026-03-07 Design feedback from Observability: prefer deterministic hashing seed derived from tenant ID for stable buckets across restarts. Added to implementation notes.
2026-03-09 Marcus Li: Opened PR #4821 (github.com/redwood-inference/observability-shim/pull/4821) with core enrichment logic and unit tests. Requesting review from eng-ingest and observability teams.

2026-03-10 QA: Integration tests added for label cap behavior using synthetic high-cardinality generator. Failing case: aggregation window boundary caused double-counting; fixed in branch and re-running.
2026-03-10 Aisha Kumar: Updated rollout plan to include automatic rollback on >2% drift in request_success_rate observed during canary.
